messages:
olivia_sre: Heads-up — we got a customer escalation call about p95/p99 getting worse for EU->US egress. Saw a noticeable jump ~01:12 UTC. Anyone else seeing it in telemetry?
lee_netops: saw the spike on infra dashboards, p95 from ~120ms -> ~420ms, p99 up to ~1.2s on a subset of clients (small payloads, many TLS handshakes).
jamal_support: Customer report: API latency spikes on ~50% of requests between eu-west1 and us-east, started around 01:10. They provided curl repros showing repeated TLS handshake durations.
alice_prod: Rolling window shows per-route tail latency increase correlated with a handful of POPs (AMS, FRA) doing egress to us-east. Not all flows affected, seems path-related.
olivia_sre: Good detail. Any recent routing/GSLB changes or DNS TTL edits around that time?
lee_netops: I deployed a GSLB weight update at 00:58 UTC to offload a saturated POP -> that touched a few DNS shards and rebalanced origin weights. TTLs are still 30s for ephemeral clients.
jamal_support: Customer says they see a lot of fresh TLS handshakes vs resumed sessions. Could be session cache miss due to sticky routing changes.
lee_netops: That tracks — weight change could cause clients to hit different egress POPs and lose session affinity. I'm pulling packet-level traces now.
olivia_sre: Can we reproduce quickly from our probing fleet?
lee_netops: Running a targeted client probe to eu-west -> us-east below:
```
# probe script
for i in {1..30}; do 
  curl -s -w "%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null https://api.redwood-inference.example/health
  sleep 0.5
done
```
lee_netops: Probe shows connect times jump between 20ms and 350ms depending on chosen egress node. Traceroute points to an extra cross-AZ hop occasionally:
```
traceroute to us-east (54.239.x.x), 30 hops max
  8  10.12.34.1  18.3 ms
  9  192.0.2.12  21.6 ms
 10  198.51.100.5  23 ms
 11  203.0.113.7  340 ms  <-- cross-region detour
 12  54.239.x.x  345 ms
```
alice_prod: That 340ms hop looks like an unexpected hairpin. Could be a peering flap or BGP path change. Any BGP churn alerts?
lee_netops: No automated BGP alerts, but GSLB change correlates timeline. Might be temporary mismatch between DNS shards and egress routing table causing suboptimal path selection.
jamal_support: Customer provided repeated curl logs with TLS handshake times ~250-900ms: they time out sometimes. They want workaround asap.
deploy-bot: NOTICE: deploy lee_netops/gslb-weight-2026-05-18 completed at 00:58 UTC (commit 9f3b2a)

olivia_sre: Action plan: 1) rollback GSLB weight tweak to pre-00:58 config (lee) 2) temporarily steer affected client prefixes to alternate POP (olivia + netops) 3) increase TLS session ticket cache size on AMS/FRA (infra) 4) collect full packet captures for one affected session (lee). Jamal, share customer repro and IPs so we can test.
lee_netops: Starting rollback now. Rolling back GSLB weights to previous commit. Will keep traffic slow-roll for 5m and monitor.
lee_netops: Rollback done at 01:22 UTC. Immediate drop in p95 to ~150ms but still noisy.
jamal_support: Sent customer IPs and curl logs to the channel DM, and confirmed they see improvement post-rollback (less timeouts).
alice_prod: Post-rollback metrics: bulk of traffic back to normal, but a subset of routes still showing 200-300ms tails — looks like some clients cached the suboptimal DNS result and keep hitting the bad path until TTL expiry.
olivia_sre: Ok, mitigations: 1) reduce DNS TTLs for the effected shards to 10s (lee) so clients re-resolve faster, 2) enable sticky session cookie/ALPN keepalive hints for clients that can use them (alice), 3) add a fallback policy to route long-handshake flows via alternate POP when handshake > 200ms (infra + runtime).
lee_netops: I'll push TTL change to 10s for the impacted shards now (scope: shards eu-1, eu-2). Rolling through within 2 minutes.
lee_netops: TTL change applied at 01:41 UTC. Expect cached clients to refresh quickly.
alice_prod: I can add a server-side heuristic in the routing layer to check recent handshake duration OC metrics and prefer lower-latency egress for those clients; I'll open a small canary for 1% of traffic.
jamal_support: Customer confirmed p99 dropped from ~1.2s -> ~350ms after rollback+TTL change. They're happy for now but want a postmortem.
olivia_sre: Notes for postmortem: timeline (GSLB weight change -> client cache -> hairpin detours -> p95/p99 spike), root cause hypothesis (weight change created transient mismatch between DNS shard mapping and egress path selection leading to hairpinning and TLS session cache loss), mitigations (rollback, TTL reduction, session cache increases, routing fallback).
lee_netops: Follow-ups: 1) add a safety for GSLB weight changes to throttle per shard (lee) 2) add automated check that verifies path-length and handshake latency after weight changes (olivia + netops) 3) verify session ticket persistence across POPs / add cross-POP session ticket sharing if feasible (infra).
alice_prod: I'll kick off a canary for the handshake-based fallback and draft the eval plan.
jamal_support: I'll coordinate with the customer for a scheduled validation window and collect any remaining traces.
olivia_sre: Good. If anyone captures a pcap/trace, drop it in the incident bucket. I'll start drafting the short postmortem and include quick-runbook steps (rollback, TTL, steer, cache-tune). :thumbsup:
lee_netops: Captured pcap for one degraded flow and uploaded to 
https://internal-logs.redwood/sre/traces/4821346790/pcap1.pcap
ollivia_sre: thanks all — marking thread closed for active mitigation, will re-open for the postmortem writeup.
